If this check is ever repeated, replay the frozen detected JSON — the cache is not the recorded run.

caveats: CORPUS TIER: every number here is _only_subset (AZ 15pp, CA 13pp, CO 10pp, TX 9pp, NV 15pp of 98, KY 8pp of 120), never full documents.
NEVER QUOTE RAW PRECISION AS QUALITY for either arm except KY, whose golden is detection-exhaustive (guardrail 8). It is reported for both arms only so the comparison is apples-to-apples.

AZ RAW PRECISION IS HIGHER FOR THE BASELINE (0.500 vs 0.417) AND THIS IS NOT A QUALITY RESULT (guardrail 7 requires reporting it anyway). Raw precision rewards under-emission: the baseline puts 8 detections in scope against AZ's 5-element spot-check golden where the LLM puts 12.

THE BASELINE'S VERIFIED PRECISION MUST NEVER APPEAR IN A TABLE BESIDE THE LLM'S. fp_audit's verdicts turn on whether a title appears in the extraction — a test for INVENTION. A rule-based extractor copies text verbatim and so scores 1.000 in five of six states by construction, against the LLM's 0.9966. Measured and recorded in baseline_comparison.json only so the claim is evidence rather than assertion.

CA IS THE ONE STATE WHERE THE BASELINE'S AUDIT IS NOT 1.000 (0.9432, 5 'hallucinated'), and all five are COLUMN FUSION rather than invention ('Using Words Discovering Use English words…'). Applied to a rule-based system that verdict detects fusion, not fabrication.

NEVER COMPARE CODE-ACCURACY RATES ACROSS ARMS. Code accuracy is graded over matched pairs only and the baseline matches far fewer elements (NV 1/3 vs 44/46 on wildly different denominators). Report matches/total for both.

THE BRITTLENESS PROBE MUST TRAVEL WITH THE HELD-OUT NUMBERS. NV 0.065 is dominated by ONE unseen token shape (SS.ID.PK1 — multi-letter code segments); widening the pattern post hoc recovers 0.522, and KY 0.295 -> 0.409 with mid-line label recognition. Neither widening is adopted, because both were motivated by inspecting the held-out states after the recorded run. Quoting the collapse without the probe overstates the result and invites the obvious objection.

TWO CONCESSIONS FAVOUR THE BASELINE and should be disclosed: it is handed detector.derive_code_from_title for elements whose code the document omits, and it emits one element per age-band column. Without the first it scores 0 on code accuracy for a schema-convention reason; without the second it cannot match any age-banded golden entry (14 of CA's 25, 4 of TX's 8).
THIS IS NOT AN EXTERNAL BASELINE. We wrote it. It is document-agnostic and held-out-disciplined, but it is not a published system and must not be described as one.
PER-STATE RECALL IS COARSE. Four of six goldens hold fewer than 10 elements, so AZ's 0.800 is 4 of 5. The pooled per-level figure (135 golden elements) is the robust one.
ONE RUN PER STATE IS SUFFICIENT HERE AND ONLY HERE — the baseline is deterministic (tests/unit/test_baseline_rule_based.py::test_it_is_deterministic). The LLM arm's stability is Task 5.

THE BASELINE'S DOMINANT FAILURE IS NOT MISCLASSIFICATION. The failure decomposition shows the missing elements are overwhelmingly never emitted at all (NV 43 of 46, KY 31 of 44), not emitted at the wrong level. Do not write the comparison as 'rules find the text but mislabel it' — that was the prior expectation and the data contradicts it.
